q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Net sales fell from ₹78,789 on 2026-10-14 to ₹68,610 on 2026-10-15 (−12.9% day‑over‑day). This sits inside the metric’s ordinary day‑to‑day range, and the diagnosis found no single upstream cause it can call causal; the data shows where the drop happened instead. (Figures are by order date.)

What changed, in order of impact
- Large increase in returns recorded on the books: P&L return revenue jumped from ₹7,285 → ₹1,27,612, which drove a big negative swing in P&L net sales and is the largest single accounting contributor to the net‑sales drop. This is an event on the P&L lines and materially reduced reported sales.
- Lower volumes and price per order: Orders fell 39 → 37 (−5.1%) and AOV fell ₹2,545 → ₹2,309 (−9.3%); together these reduced net sales by the remainder of the movement.
- Ad spend was lower (₹47,393 → ₹38,025, −19.8%) but stayed within its normal range and was tested/ruled out as an unusual cause; sessions and web events also moved together with sales but do not establish causation.

Worth checking: investigate the large same‑day jump in return/cancel revenue (by product and by order) and the handful of campaigns/ad names that showed outsized swings (e.g. TH‑068… entries called out in the data).
